entries.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Victoria 3 TECHNOLOGY illustration, square transparent PNG, at least 1024 pixels. Not a flat PM pictogram.
Input images: Image 1 is the rejected wooden hull icon to REBUILD; Image 2 (native frigate) and Image 3 (native steelworking) are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY, do not copy their subjects.
Primary request: remake the wooden diagonal ship framing as a structurally readable compact midship hull cutaway. Retain the warm oak material and painted game-icon identity, but completely replace the faulty brace arrangement.
Structural layout: one short section of a wooden ship, with THREE evenly spaced transverse U-shaped rib frames connected by an integral keel and longitudinal hull planks. Every rib curves smoothly across the bottom from its near-side upright to its far-side upright; all frames share a coherent boat cross-section and perspective. Low near-side planking is cut away to expose the structure. The back inner SIDE WALL has two broad DIAGONAL TIMBER RIDERS laid AGAINST that curved inner hull surface, diagonally across several transverse ribs from a lower position at one longitudinal station to an upper position at another. Their joints seat visibly against the ribs and longitudinal timber. The diagonals run FORE-AND-AFT along the inside side of the hull, not across the open middle from one side to the other. Keep the open central interior completely clear. No giant ramps spanning the bowl, no roof-truss beams, no two timbers crossing unsupported in empty space, no floaters or incompatible joints. The long back-side diagonal strokes are the strongest identifying feature. The curved rib frames make this unmistakably a boat section, not a timber wall or house frame.
Composition: slightly elevated three-quarter longitudinal view looking into the inside side of the hull, one compact complete object centered with 8-10 percent clear transparent margins. Prioritize a few connected large members over intricate small woodwork, readable at 48/64 pixels. Conceptual simplified illustration informed by museum model SLR2908; not an exact engineering reconstruction.
Style: restrained HAND-PAINTED volumetric object, broad clear planes, subtle brushed oak grain, warm natural honey-brown oak with darker side faces and short restrained highlights. No glossy photoreal 3D model, global blue cast or gold filter. No pedestals, supports, background scene, display table, modern fasteners, metal hull, sails, mast, guns, tools, books, people or added props.
Transparency: genuine alpha outside the object AND through all exposed gaps with no backing panel or painted black backdrop. Solid wood and planks remain opaque. No baked cast-shadow patch, UI frame, surrounding circle or border. No text, letters, digits, labels, signatures, watermark. Deliver just ONE finished icon.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: Victoria 3 TECHNOLOGY illustration, square transparent PNG, at least 1024 pixels. Not a flat PM pictogram.
Input images: Image 1 is the iron hull EDIT TARGET. Image 2 (native frigate) and Image 3 (native steelworking) are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY, not additional objects.
Primary request: correct ONLY the exposed framing on the LEFT open cutaway of the hull. It currently has inconsistent half-ribs, arbitrary capped tops, misaligned horizontal members and ambiguous joints. Reconstruct this small region into a physically coherent, SIMPLER connected iron skeleton.
Correction: show TWO evenly spaced transverse U-shaped forged angle-iron rib frames at two separate fore-and-aft stations. Each frame has one continuous, consistent section curving from its near gunwale end, down around the bilge and bottom, then up its FAR SIDE; every rib's path can be understood. Far-side portions may be naturally occluded by the solid plated hull, but never end floating in space. The bottom of each U joins the existing integral keel at a clearly seated connection. Both frame stations have compatible curvature, height, thickness and perspective. Use a single slim longitudinal rail joining their upper ends on the near side, and a matching rail on the far side only where visible. These rails terminate flush against the attached shell framing with a simple riveted joint. REMOVE the weird extra rib, isolated T-caps, ladder-like crossbars, thin floating shelf, protruding disconnected horizontal strips and changes of beam section along a single curve. No new diagonal braces. Every visible member must attach to something and never intersect impossibly. This is a short iron hull section, not a chair, a fence or stacked disconnected loops.
Invariants: preserve the LARGE RIGHT-HAND PLATED BOW, its shape, neutral grey iron palette, rivet rows, seams, patina, existing camera angle, lighting and overall scale. Do not redesign that successful plated area or add/remove other objects. Changes to its left attachment seam are allowed only to join the corrected rib frames. Keep the same painted volumetric technology style, muted charcoal/grey with slight brown wear and restrained glints; no blue tint, gold wash or glossy chrome.
Framing/background: full object within a square, centered with transparent margins; true alpha in all open spaces, no black fill, floor, water, cast-shadow patch, frame, medallion or UI tile. Solid iron remains opaque. No annotation marks, red circles, arrows, labels, text, digits, watermark or signature. No wood, armor turret, cabin, machinery, tools, scenery or accessories. Deliver one finished corrected icon.
